html:
The Karluks were a Turkic tribal confederation of Central Asia, first living near the Altai and the Black Irtysh, later in the Zhetysu, the land of seven rivers south of Lake Balkhash. The map shows them in 700, 800 and 900.

They were subjects of the Türk Khaganates. In 742 they joined the Uyghurs and the Basmyl to destroy the Second Turkic Khaganate, then fell out with the Uyghurs and moved west. In the Battle of Talas of 751, between the Tang and the Abbasid Caliphate, Karluk troops are said to have switched to the Arab side, helping to decide it. Around 766 they took the Zhetysu and its towns.

Many historians think the Karluks led the Kara-Khanid state that rose in the 900s, whose khan Satuq Bughra was the first Turkic ruler to turn Muslim. Their descendants are among today's Uzbeks and Uyghurs.
